title: sagina procumbens subsp. littoralis
intro: Sagina procumbens subsp. littoralis, commonly known as marsh sagina, is a type of flowering plant native to Europe, Asia, and North Africa. It is known for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which may help to soothe and calm irritated skin and mucous membranes. The therapeutic actions of marsh sagina are thought to be due to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which have been shown to have anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects. However, more research is needed to confirm the health benefits and therapeutic actions of this plant, but it has been traditionally used in herbal medicine to treat a range of ailments, including digestive issues and respiratory problems.
